what_happened: Research for the restack-on-merge phase found every git primitive already present and exercised elsewhere in review-stack-prepare.sh (merge-tree, merge-base, commit-tree, update-ref, symbolic-ref), plus a directly reusable detection/recompute function (rsp_move_commit_onto_new_parent) and reusable no-push/no-fetch test-fixture technique from Phase 3's cases; no blocker, workaround, or deviation from the dispatch's own description arose.

The parent plan's Phase 4 Scope Hypothesis and Tier Justification both predicted the touched-path selector would return __FULL_SWEEP__ for this phase's two paths because neither file existed at parent-authoring time. Both now exist; re-running verify-touched.sh over the whole Files-to-modify set in one invocation resolved to exactly one real suite (test-review-stack-prepare.sh), no sentinel, exit 0. Every Tier Justification in this plan names the measured result instead of the inherited prediction.

All four measurable claims in the dispatch description verified unchanged against live state before planning: 38 passing suite cases (live run), exit codes contiguous through 52 (header table lines 94-119), no restack dispatch arm (dispatcher lines 1204-1218), both static assertions green. The research report's three PD7 ambiguity readings were adoptable verbatim as plan decisions D1-D3, which removed all improvisation risk from the implement phase.
